citations.title: Licensing Procedures
citations.requirement: The applicant must be 21 or older and disclose owners of 25% or more, prior license actions, and criminal charges and Medicare/Medicaid violations. The application needs a business plan (1-year budget, populations served, services), the .08B policies, proof of workers' compensation, and a $1,000 nonrefundable fee for a 3-year license. A license is valid 3 years. Renewal needs a $1,000 fee, substantively changed policies (complaints, client evaluation), valid licenses and certificates for current employees, and an annual data collection survey. OHCQ may inspect before deciding, may approve with conditions (management firm up to 24 months, or a term under 1 year), and may issue provisional licenses. It may charge $250 per additional pre-licensure visit.

citations.title: Administration
citations.requirement: The agency must have a governing authority that meets at least annually with management to review and advise on policies and keeps minutes (participants, agenda, actions). It must develop and implement policies on: scope of services, care coordination, admission criteria, pre-acceptance assessment, billing and service records, QA, and clinical management (assessment, plans, delegation, supervision). It also needs policies on job descriptions and qualifications, skill assessments, and employee health requirements. Patient care policies cover skilled-service criteria, administration of drugs, frequency of client monitoring, and training of clients and families. Informed consent policies cover plan-of-care changes and routine treatments or medication self-administration by non-licensed staff. Environment and safety policies cover infection control, biomedical waste, equipment, and emergency procedures. OHCQ may waive a policy if the agency gives a written explanation.

citations.title: Complaint Process
citations.requirement: The agency needs an internal complaint process with client notice, investigation protocols, and timely handling of written complaints without disrupting services. Each investigation report states time, date, place and people involved, a full description, the disposition, and follow-up to prevent recurrence. If no investigation is done, the reason must be documented. The agency notifies the client or representative, the physician if needed, and licensing or law enforcement agencies when required. Clients must be given OHCQ's complaint hotline number. Investigation reports go to OHCQ immediately on request, and a public summary is available on request as permitted by law.

citations.title: Employee, Independent Contractor, and Contractual Employee Requirements
citations.requirement: Pre-referral screening must include: criminal history check (State or private) under Health-General Title 19, Subtitle 19; licensure or certification verification; basic health screening including TB; references; employment history; I-9; identity and employment eligibility; an in-person interview; and a skills assessment and demonstration. Training records go in the personnel file, and screening records are kept in the agency's business office. A non-certified caregiver may be provided only if the client needs no ADL help, only needs ADL help with no predictable adverse health consequences in the supervising nurse's judgment, or signs a waiver of skilled services. A certified caregiver is required for clients who need one for ADLs or for medication administration. Conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action must be reported immediately to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ. Subcontract agencies must verify personnel information and give evidence of that to the contracting agency.

citations.title: Training
citations.requirement: Referred individuals must be appropriately trained. Outside trainers need OHCQ's written approval. Minimum content for in-home care: instruction and supervised practice in personal care; recognizing situations that need RN referral, including significant change in condition; record keeping; ethics and confidentiality; CPR; standard precautions; and prevention of abuse and neglect.

citations.title: Services Provided
citations.requirement: An RN assesses each new client who requires skilled services and ADL help, helps develop the plan of care and assign staff, decides whether a CNA is needed, and helps train staff. Assessment is required: when services are requested; before services start (with limited exceptions); within 48 hours for listed skilled needs or a significant change of condition (7 calendar days if the RN documents the 48-hour assessment is unnecessary); on client request; and at least annually. The care plan must state services, when and how often, who provides them and how, long- and short-range goals, and safety measures. Informed consent and waivers need a documented risk/benefit discussion, a signed and dated form, and a copy in the record. RN on-site supervision is required at least every 45 days if staff administer medications, every 3 months if staff assist with self-administration, and every 4 months otherwise, or more often as the RN decides. Supervision must be documented. Medication administration requires licensed or certified staff, physician orders, and documentation of medications, errors and adverse reactions. On-call: 24/7 contact, response within 1 hour, a call log, and written on-call procedures given to clients.

citations.title: Client Representative
citations.requirement: The agency must recognize a guardian of the person or property, an advance directive, a surrogate decision maker, a power of attorney, a representative payee, or a person designated in writing by a competent client. It may not honor a representative who exceeds the authority granted. It must document the representative's name or keep the authorizing document in the record.

citations.title: Maintenance of Records
citations.requirement: Client records are kept 5 years after discharge. For minors, keep until age 21 or 5 years after the record is made, whichever is later. If the agency closes, records must be returned to the client or representative or retained as required. Records are confidential and released only with written consent or as permitted by Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3. Discharged client records must be completed within 30 days of discharge. Safeguards must protect against loss, destruction and unauthorized use.

citations.title: Client's Rights and Responsibilities
citations.requirement: Written rights policies must be available to clients. Clients must receive: a cost estimate; a statement of costs not covered by third parties; itemized bills on request; the caregiver's name; the name and contact of the care supervisor; the 24/7 phone number; and disclosure of subcontractual relationships. Rights include dignity, participation in the care plan, refusing treatment, privacy, freedom from abuse, neglect, involuntary seclusion and exploitation, confidentiality, and complaints without retaliation with a prompt response. Clients must have access to complaint procedures for OHCQ and for Adult or Child Protective Services. The agency must give advance directive information and obtain the client's advance directive information. It must honor refusal of treatment and waivers of skilled services. Informed consent information must cover purpose, alternatives, side effects and benefits, cost, and the right to withdraw. Clients may accept or reject any referred caregiver without retaliation.

citations.title: Conditions for Provider Participation — General Requirements
citations.requirement: The provider must meet the COMAR 10.09.36 Medicaid conditions and obtain written verification of worker qualifications. Incidents and complaints are reported within 24 hours of knowledge, with a written report within 7 calendar days on the Department's form. The local department of social services is notified immediately of suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation (COMAR 07.02.16). The provider must cooperate with inspections, reviews and audits. It bills only services preauthorized in the plan of service, delivered consistent with it, and within the provider agreement. Service documentation (dates and hours) is kept 6 years from date of service. Services may not be suspended, terminated, increased or reduced without Department authorization and consultation with the participant, and a transition plan goes to the case manager or supports planner and participant. Medicaid eligibility is verified at the start of each month of service. The provider may not have unpaid overpayments and must be free of conflicts of interest. Providers and principals must be free of 24-month look-back events: license suspension or revocation, Medicaid suspension or sanction, disciplinary action, State deficiency citations affecting health and safety, and agreement terminations.

citations.title: Specific Conditions for Provider Participation — Personal Assistance
citations.requirement: The provider must hold an RSA license (the text says to provide 'Level Two or Level Three home care services') and employ an RN. The RN assesses each new participant, helps develop worker instructions and assign staff, delegates nursing tasks to a CNA or CMT under COMAR 10.27.11, and instructs workers. Workers must accept instruction on the plan of service from the participant or representative, the nurse monitor, a treating physician or NP, or MDH. Participants must have a significant role in directing services, including selecting, training, scheduling, setting duties for and dismissing their worker. The provider gives MDH 45 days' written notice of closure, change of ownership, location, name or tax ID, or sale, including how participants will be informed and a transition plan. It must apply for a new license on a transfer of ownership. It collects the participant's (or representative's) signature at least monthly verifying services. Criminal history checks are required for all direct service workers, including nurses. Workers who administer medications must be CMTs, and workers who perform other delegated nursing functions must also be CNAs. The participant's representative may not be assigned as the worker.

citations.title: Payment Procedures
citations.requirement: To be paid for personal assistance, the provider and its workers must use the Department-approved telephonic timekeeping system to document time and submit claims. Billing time limits come from COMAR 10.09.36.06. The provider is paid the lesser of its usual and customary charge to the general public or the fee schedule rate. Services up to 12 hours/day are paid in 15-minute units, and a daily rate applies above 12 hours. The Department publishes the fee schedule at least annually. Rates rise 3% each July 1, subject to the State budget.

citations.title: Covered Services — Personal Assistance
citations.requirement: Defines the covered personal assistance services (ADL/IADL help per the plan of service). Section text was not re-fetched in this pass; it comes from the supplied fact-checked research (S36).

citations.title: Limitations
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S57): services are limited to a service budget based on assessed need. Escort and travel expenses are not covered, and housekeeping unrelated to ADLs is not covered.

citations.title: Participant Eligibility
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S35): institutional level of care, Medicaid eligibility, and living at home are required. The plan of service names the personal assistance agency the participant chooses.

citations.title: Nurse Monitoring providers
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S37): nurse monitoring providers are designated by the Department under §1915(b)(4). The agency coordinates with the participant's nurse monitor.

citations.title: Covered Services — Nurse Monitoring
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S56): nurse monitoring contact every 6 months and an in-person visit every 12 months. Agency staff must cooperate with the nurse monitor.

citations.title: CPAS — Specific Conditions for Provider Participation — Personal Assistance
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S49): CPAS personal assistance providers must hold an RSA license, employ an RN, and meet the parallel participation conditions that apply to CFC.

citations.title: Billing Time Limitations
citations.requirement: Referenced in COMAR 10.09.84.24C as the source of Medicaid billing time limits. The 12-month claim limit comes from the CFC Billing Manual (C37). The section text was not fetched.

citations.title: Cause for Suspension or Removal and Imposition of Sanctions
citations.requirement: Referenced in COMAR 10.09.84.05B(3) and in PT 13-27 as the basis for Medicaid suspension, removal and sanctions. The section text was not fetched.

citations.title: RSA worker-classification certification for personal care aides
citations.requirement: Per the OHCQ RSA page (research S1): the person who controls pay and employment practices must read the RSA-PCA Guidance Document and submit the online RSA Certification form. This is a condition of obtaining and keeping the license.

citations.title: Criminal history records checks for direct service workers
citations.requirement: Cited in COMAR 10.07.05.10B(1)(a) and 10.09.84.06A(11) as the procedure for State criminal history records checks (or private agency background checks) on direct service workers, including nurses.

citations.title: Adult Protective Services
citations.requirement: Cited in COMAR 10.09.84.05A(3)(c) as the basis for immediately notifying the local department of social services when there is reason to believe a participant has been subjected to abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation. Only the cross-reference was verified. The chapter text was not fetched.

citations.title: Residential Service Agencies Provider Compliance Audits (Aug. 10, 2026)
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S38): DPICC audits RSAs, and non-responders are suspended after three outreach attempts. Respond to a plan of correction within 15 calendar days. Repeat findings within 6 months can bring sanctions under COMAR 10.09.36.

citations.title: Updates for the Home and Community-Based Services Cost Survey
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S12): the annual HCBS Cost Survey is due Dec. 31, 2026. Payment is suspended from Jan. 1, 2027 for non-filers.

citations.title: MPRIME Launch — Day One Provider Actions and Enrollment Policy Updates
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S39): MPRIME went live Oct. 13, 2026. A complete application by Dec. 31, 2026 can be backdated. An SDAT ID in good standing is required, and MPRIME auto-suspends providers that lose it. License uploads are due by March 31, 2027, and expired licenses trigger suspension from April 1, 2027.

citations.title: FY 2025 Rates for CFC and CPAS (effective July 1, 2024)
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S9, S14, S15): W5519 (CFC) and W5527 (CPAS) are $6.3962 per 15-minute unit. Shared attendant is $4.2597 per 15 minutes (W5521/W5528). The daily rate for more than 12 hours per day is $329.84 (W5532). Rates were reported unchanged as of July 1, 2025 and level in the FY 2027 budget.

citations.title: Federal EVV requirement for Medicaid personal care services
citations.requirement: Federal requirement for electronic visit verification of Medicaid personal care services. Maryland meets it through the state telephonic system (ISAS).

citations.title: Ensuring Access to Medicaid Services rule — payment adequacy and rate transparency
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S43): an 80% direct-care compensation standard, applicable from July 9, 2030 per MDH's 2024 report, plus rate transparency. RSAs must also file an annual personal care aide wage report with the Department of Labor by Sept. 1 (HB 189/SB 371 of 2024).

citations.cite: Maryland Minimum Wage and Overtime Law (MDOL guidance)
citations.title: Maryland Minimum Wage and Overtime Law
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S21): the State minimum is $15.00 and overtime is due after 40 hours. Howard County is $16.00. Montgomery County from July 1, 2026 is $16.50 for home care employers with 11+ employees that get at least 75% of gross revenue from Medicaid, and otherwise $18.00 (51+ employees), $16.50 (11–50) or $15.95 (10 or fewer). No statute section number is cited because none was verified.

citations.cite: Maryland Healthy Working Families Act (MDOL FAQs)
citations.title: Earned Sick and Safe Leave
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S27): 1 hour accrues per 30 hours worked, with a 40-hour annual accrual. Leave is paid for employers with 15+ employees. Statutory caps beyond that should be confirmed with MDOL before the policy is finalized.

citations.cite: Maryland Workers' Compensation Commission — Questions and Answers for Employers
citations.title: Workers' compensation coverage
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S26): every employer with one or more employees must provide workers' compensation coverage. Proof is also required for the RSA application under COMAR 10.07.05.04A(2)(j).

citations.title: Changes in an Agency That Affect the Operating License
citations.requirement: The section exists per the chapter table of contents. Its text was not fetched. The OHCQ RSA page (S1) requires 45 days' written notice of a change of ownership and has separate forms for added services, address, name and branch changes.

citations.title: Public Representation
citations.requirement: The section exists per the chapter table of contents and governs how the agency represents itself publicly. Its text was not fetched. Read it before finalizing advertising wording.

citations.title: Inspection by the Department
citations.requirement: The section exists per the chapter table of contents and governs OHCQ inspections. Its text was not fetched.

citations.title: Clinical Records
citations.requirement: The section exists per the chapter table of contents and governs clinical record content. Its text could not be fetched. Confirm required record elements before finalizing the record-content checklist.

citations.title: Community First Choice Billing Manual
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S10): personal assistance is documented and paid through ISAS, which generates claims. Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service.

citations.title: ISAS provider training
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S46): participant primary landline or OTP device verification, up to 5 admin and 5 billing roles, a missing-time limit of 4 requests due within 2 business days after month-end, a Thursday–Wednesday workweek, and help desk 1-855-463-5877. These details are from 2020 training, so confirm them with the ISAS Help Desk.

citations.cite: OLTSS SOP — Standardized Times for Assistance with ADLs, IADLs and Delegated Nursing Tasks (rev. April 29, 2025)
citations.title: Standardized task times
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S51): OLTSS standard times used when planning and authorizing assistance with ADLs, IADLs and delegated nursing tasks.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S4): defines residential service agency, home health care, certified care and ADLs/IADLs. A residential service agency employs or contracts workers to provide at least one home health care service to an unrelated sick or disabled person at home.

citations.title: Replacement of Personal Emergency Response Systems
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S50): lists Maryland Access Point (1-844-MAP-LINK) and OLTSS (410-767-1739) as contacts for PERS and community resources.

policies.title: Governing Authority, Organization, Administrator Responsibilities and Policy Review
state_specifics: Governing authority meets at least annually with management to review and advise on policies; minutes record participants, agenda and actions
Policies are reviewed at least annually; each revision is dated, versioned and approved in the minutes
Changed policies (complaints, client evaluation) must be submitted with the 3-year renewal
OHCQ may waive a required policy only on a written explanation from the agency
COMAR 10.07.05 sets no administrator credential; the agency names a responsible administrator and an RN

policies.title: Scope of Services — What Caregivers May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Agency provides non-medical home health aide/personal care: ADL and IADL help per the RN plan of care or Medicaid plan of service
Services are limited to the service budget based on assessed need (COMAR 10.09.84.23)
Escort and travel expenses and housekeeping unrelated to ADLs are not covered by Medicaid
Caregivers perform nursing tasks only when delegated by the RN to a CNA/CMT, never on their own
Services outside the scope require an RN assessment or referral

policies.title: Care Coordination and Delineation of Services Provided by the Agency and Other Providers
state_specifics: Written list of what the agency provides directly versus what other providers (home health agency, nurse monitor, physician, supports planner) provide
When another provider supplies skilled care, the RN documents who does what and shares the plan
Subcontracted services are disclosed to the client in writing (COMAR 10.07.05.16)
Coordination contacts are logged in the client record

policies.title: Notification of Agency Care-Coordination Responsibilities to Client or Representative
state_specifics: At admission the client or the representative with legal authority to make health care decisions is told in writing what the agency will and will not coordinate
The representative's name is documented, or the authorizing document (guardianship, advance directive, POA, surrogate) is kept in the record
The agency does not honor a representative acting beyond granted authority
Notice is repeated when coordination duties change

policies.title: Admission Criteria and Client Intake
state_specifics: Written admission criteria: need is within agency scope, safe home environment, staff available, RN can supervise
Medicaid clients: institutional level of care, Medicaid eligibility and living at home; plan of service names the agency
Medicaid eligibility is verified at the start of each month of service
Declined referrals are documented with the reason and a referral to MAP (1-844-MAP-LINK) or other resources
Client may accept or reject any referred caregiver without retaliation

policies.title: Pre-Acceptance Assessment of Potential Clients
state_specifics: RN assesses each new client who needs ADL help and decides whether a CNA is needed
Assessment is required when services are requested and before services start, with limited exceptions
Assessment covers ADLs/IADLs, medications, home safety, risks and client goals
OLTSS standard task times are used when planning Medicaid-authorized assistance

policies.title: Billing, Service Records and Charges
state_specifics: Private pay: written cost estimate up front, statement of costs not covered by third parties, itemized bill on request
Medicaid billing: only services preauthorized in the plan of service and delivered consistent with it
Medicaid pays the lesser of the usual and customary charge or the fee schedule rate; 15-minute units up to 12 hours/day, daily rate above
Claims are generated through ISAS; submit within 12 months of date of service
For managed-care or third-party clients, records are kept as that payer requires

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Written QA program reviewed at the annual governing authority meeting
Indicators: complaints, incidents, missed visits, supervisory visit timeliness, ISAS exceptions, record audits
Findings produce documented corrective actions
Annual OHCQ data collection survey is completed at renewal
Self-audit mirrors DPICC audit categories (PT 13-27)

policies.title: Clinical Management: Assessment, Plans of Care, Delegation
state_specifics: RN reassesses at least annually, on client request, and within 48 hours of listed skilled needs or significant change (7 calendar days if RN documents 48 hours is unnecessary)
Plan of care states services, when and how often, who provides them and how, long- and short-range goals, and safety measures
Delegation of nursing tasks only to CNA/CMT under COMAR 10.27.11, documented by the RN
Agency employs the RN (required for CFC/CPAS)
Workers take plan instruction from the participant, nurse monitor, treating physician/NP or MDH

policies.title: RN Supervision, Supervisory Visits and 24/7 On-Call
state_specifics: RN on-site supervision at least every 45 days if staff administer medications; every 3 months if staff assist with self-administration; every 4 months otherwise
Every supervisory visit is documented; the RN may visit more often
24/7 client contact with response within 1 hour
On-call log kept; written on-call procedures and phone number given to each client
Missed or late supervisory visits are reported to the administrator

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area, Advertising and Changes Affecting the License
state_specifics: RSA license is valid 3 years; renewal fee $1,000 plus renewal documents
Worker-classification certification (Health-General §19-4A-11) is required to obtain and keep the license
45 days' written notice to OHCQ and Medicaid before change of ownership, location, name, tax ID or closure; new owner applies for a new license
Advertising describes only services listed on the license; review COMAR 10.07.05.06 before publishing

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Bill only services delivered and documented in ISAS per the plan of service
No unpaid overpayments and no conflicts of interest to remain a Medicaid provider
DPICC audit responses; plan of correction due within 15 calendar days; non-responders suspended after three outreach attempts
Annual PCA wage report to the Department of Labor by September 1
Principals screened against the 24-month look-back events (COMAR 10.09.84.05B)

policies.title: Medicaid Provider Participation, Enrollment and Cost Survey (CFC/CPAS, PT 76)
state_specifics: MPRIME enrollment as PT 76; SDAT ID must stay in good standing or MPRIME auto-suspends
Upload RSA license by March 31, 2027 and after each renewal; expired license triggers suspension from April 1, 2027
HCBS Cost Survey due December 31, 2026; non-filers suspended from January 1, 2027
Rates: W5519/W5527 $6.3962 per 15 min; shared attendant $4.2597; daily rate over 12 hrs $329.84
Contacts: MPRIME 1-844-463-7768; OLTSS 410-767-1739

policies.title: Job Descriptions and Educational Qualifications for Employees and Contractors
state_specifics: Written job descriptions with required education, license or certification for administrator, RN, CNA, CMT, aide, scheduler
RN must hold a current Maryland license
Medication administration roles require CMT or licensed staff
Aides doing delegated nursing tasks must be CNAs; the participant's representative may not be assigned as the worker

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Certified vs. Non-Certified Caregivers and Worker Classification
state_specifics: Certified caregiver required for clients needing one for ADLs or medication administration
Non-certified caregiver only if no ADL need, ADL need with no predictable adverse consequences in the RN's judgment, or signed waiver of skilled services
Aides are classified as W-2 employees unless counsel advises otherwise
Worker-classification certification form kept on file

policies.title: Pre-Referral Screening, Criminal History Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Before referral: State or private criminal history check under Health-General Title 19, Subtitle 19, license/certification verification, references, employment history, I-9, identity, in-person interview, skills demonstration
Criminal history checks apply to all direct service workers including nurses
Conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action is reported immediately to the Board and OHCQ
Screening records are kept in the agency's business office
Medicaid requires written verification of worker qualifications

policies.title: Skill Assessments of Employees and Contractors
state_specifics: Skills assessment and demonstration are completed before the first client assignment
RN observes or verifies personal care skills; checklist signed and dated
Reassessment on annual review and after performance concerns
Results kept in the personnel file

policies.title: Health Requirements and TB Screening for Employees and Contractors
state_specifics: Basic health screening including TB before referral to any client
Hepatitis B vaccine offered per OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard
Staff with communicable illness are excluded from client contact until cleared
Health records kept apart from the main personnel file

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual Training
state_specifics: Minimum content: personal care skills with supervised practice, recognizing when to call the RN (significant change), record keeping, ethics and confidentiality, CPR, standard precautions, abuse and neglect prevention
Outside trainers need OHCQ written approval before training
Add ISAS clock-in/out training and HIPAA training
Training records go in each personnel file

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Screening and personnel records are kept in the agency's business office
Each file holds screening results, license/certification, health screen, training records, I-9, skills assessment
Current professional licenses of all employees are verified at license renewal
Files are retained at least 6 years to match Medicaid audit exposure

policies.title: Wage, Hour, Overtime and Leave Compliance
state_specifics: State minimum $15.00; Howard County $16.00; Montgomery County from July 1, 2026 is $16.50 for home care employers with 11+ employees and at least 75% Medicaid revenue, otherwise $18.00/$16.50/$15.95 by size
Overtime after 40 hours; travel time between clients counts as work time where required
Earned sick and safe leave: 1 hour per 30 worked; paid at 15+ employees
Workers' compensation required for every employer with one or more employees
Annual PCA wage report to the Department of Labor by September 1

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Training covers ethics and confidentiality
No gifts, loans, financial transactions or use of client property
No personal-phone matching client phone in ISAS verification
Clients may reject any caregiver without retaliation
Violations lead to discipline and, if abuse or exploitation, mandatory reporting

policies.title: Independent Contractors, Contractual Employees and Subcontract Agencies
state_specifics: Contractors meet the same screening, training and health requirements as employees
Subcontract agencies verify personnel information and give evidence to the contracting agency
Subcontract relationships are disclosed to clients
Classification of aides is reviewed against Health-General §19-4A-11 guidance

policies.title: Provision of Home Health Care Services and Criteria for Determining Need for Skilled Services
state_specifics: Agency provides home health aide/personal care; skilled nursing is provided only if listed on the OHCQ license
RN applies written criteria to decide skilled need at assessment and on change in condition
Skilled need identified: assessment within 48 hours (7 days if RN documents), then refer, coordinate or deliver by RN
Client who declines recommended skilled care signs a waiver after a risk/benefit discussion

policies.title: Service Plan (Plan of Care/Plan of Service) and Plan Updates
state_specifics: Medicaid plan of service names and is signed by the agency; schedule must not exceed authorized hours
Plan states services, frequency, who provides them, goals and safety measures
Reassess at least annually, on request and on significant change
Participant directs services: selects, trains, schedules and dismisses worker
Changes in service are made only with Department authorization for Medicaid clients

policies.title: Medication Assistance, Self-Administration Support and Administration of Drugs
state_specifics: Default: aides assist only with self-administration after client consent
Administration requires licensed or certified staff (CMT for CFC), physician orders and documentation of medications, errors and adverse reactions
RN supervision interval is 45 days if staff administer, 3 months if assisting with self-administration
Medication errors and adverse reactions are reported to the RN and recorded
Non-licensed assistance needs signed informed consent

policies.title: Enteral and Parenteral Nutrition Procedures
state_specifics: Agency does not provide enteral (tube) or parenteral (IV) nutrition; aides must not perform or manage it
Clients who need it are referred to a licensed provider; RN documents the referral
Adding the service requires an RN-written procedure, an RSA license service update with OHCQ and a revision of this manual
Aides report any tube/line problems to the RN and call 911 in emergencies

policies.title: Frequency of Client Monitoring
state_specifics: RN on-site every 45 days / 3 months / 4 months per medication involvement, or more often if RN decides
Reassessment at least annually and on significant change
Medicaid nurse monitor contacts participant every 6 months with an in-person visit every 12 months; agency cooperates
Monitoring schedule is set at the first RN assessment and recorded in the plan

policies.title: Training and Retraining of Clients and Family Members
state_specifics: RN identifies training needs (safe transfers, equipment, medication self-administration, infection precautions)
Training and teach-back are documented in the record
Retraining when condition, equipment or caregivers change
Participants who direct their own workers are trained on that role

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Schedule no more than authorized plan-of-service hours
Missed visits: notify client, arrange replacement, notify RN if health or safety at risk
Shared-attendant codes (W5521/W5528) when an aide serves two participants
Services may not be suspended, terminated, increased or reduced without Department authorization
Clients may reject a caregiver without retaliation

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification (ISAS) and Timekeeping
state_specifics: Aides clock in and out by phone at the start and end of each shift; ISAS is the only way to bill personal assistance
Verification from participant's primary landline or OTP device; the aide's phone must never match the client's
Up to 5 admin and 5 billing roles; aides cannot log in to the portal
Per 2020 training: 4 missing-time requests, due 2 business days after month end, Thursday–Wednesday workweek; confirm with help desk 1-855-463-5877
Time over plan hours is reduced automatically and unpaid

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Aides are trained to recognize significant change and call the RN
Call 911 first in emergencies, then RN and family or representative
RN assesses within 48 hours of significant change (7 calendar days if documented as unnecessary)
Advance directive information is checked and honored
Incidents are reported under the incident policy

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: Medicaid services are not ended or reduced without Department authorization and consultation with the participant
Transition plan goes to case manager or supports planner and participant
Closure or sale requires 45 days' notice to MDH with a client transition plan
Discharged record is completed within 30 days

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs, Nurse Monitors and Payers
state_specifics: Monthly Medicaid eligibility check at the start of each service month
Cooperate with supports planners, nurse monitors and MDH/OLTSS inspections and audits
PERS and community referrals via MAP 1-844-MAP-LINK; OLTSS 410-767-1739
Participant or representative signs at least monthly verifying services

policies.title: Informed Consent to Changes in the Agency's Recommended Plan of Care
state_specifics: Client or representative with legal authority signs informed consent when changing the recommended plan
Documented risk/benefit discussion; signed and dated form; copy in the record
Information covers purpose, alternatives, side effects and benefits, cost and right to withdraw
Refusal of treatment is honored without retaliation

policies.title: Consent to Assistance by Non-Licensed Staff with Routine Treatments and Self-Administration of Medications
state_specifics: Client signs consent before non-licensed staff assist with routine treatments or medication self-administration
Consent form lists the tasks and is kept in the record
Consent is reviewed at each annual reassessment
Client may withdraw consent at any time

policies.title: Waiver of Skilled Services and Certified Caregiver
state_specifics: Waiver is allowed only for a client who has capacity or a representative with authority, after RN risk/benefit discussion
Signed and dated waiver form; copy in record
Agency honors waivers
RN reviews waiver at each reassessment

policies.title: Client Representatives and Advance Directives
state_specifics: Recognize guardian, advance directive, surrogate, POA, representative payee or person designated in writing by a competent client
Do not honor a representative exceeding granted authority
Document the representative's name or keep the authorizing document
Provide advance directive information and obtain client's advance directive information

policies.title: Preparation and Storage of Enteral Formulas, IV Therapies, Supplies and Equipment
state_specifics: Agency does not prepare or store enteral formulas or IV therapies; aides must not handle them
Routine client supplies are stored clean, dry and separate from food
Aides report supplies problems to the RN
If these services are added, a preparation and storage procedure must be written first

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Standard precautions training required
Hand hygiene, gloves, cleaning and laundry procedures
Exposure incident procedure and sharps rules
Staff with symptoms stay out of client homes
Written exposure control plan under OSHA

policies.title: Disposal of Biomedical Waste
state_specifics: Agency does not generate biomedical waste; aides do not handle sharps
Contaminated items are double-bagged and disposed of in household trash only when the RN confirms it is permitted
Sharps are never recapped or handled; RN is called
Any needlestick is reported as an exposure incident

policies.title: Maintenance of Equipment
state_specifics: Agency-owned equipment (e.g., gait belts, lifts if used) is inspected and cleaned between clients
Client-owned equipment: aides report malfunctions to the RN and do not repair it
Defective equipment is removed from use and documented
PERS replacement questions go to MAP or OLTSS

policies.title: Emergency Procedures, Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: Each client has an emergency/disaster plan at intake (evacuation, medical, power outage)
Agency emergency procedures cover office closure, staff shortage and severe weather
24/7 on-call line with 1-hour response
Priority list of clients at highest risk
Backup caregivers identified for each client

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Home safety review at assessment
Caregivers may leave an unsafe home and must call the supervisor
Violence and threats are reported as incidents
Training covers body mechanics and safe transfers

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Escort and travel expenses are not covered by Medicaid personal assistance
Private-pay transport only if in the service agreement, with valid license and insurance
Non-owned auto coverage should be in place
Aides do not transport clients in their own vehicle for Medicaid-covered time

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation is reported immediately to the local department of social services (COMAR 07.02.16)
Clients are free from abuse, neglect, involuntary seclusion and exploitation
Incident also reported within 24 hours for Medicaid clients
Staff are trained on prevention and reporting; retaliation is prohibited
OHCQ hotline 800-492-6005

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: Report incidents and complaints within 24 hours of knowledge for Medicaid clients
Written report within 7 calendar days on the Department's form
Investigation records time, date, place, people, description, disposition and follow-up
Notify the client or representative, physician if needed and licensing or law enforcement as required

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Written rights policy available to clients
Rights include dignity, participation in the care plan, refusing treatment, privacy, confidentiality and freedom from abuse and exploitation
Complaint without retaliation with prompt response
Provide caregiver name, care supervisor name and contact, and 24/7 phone number
Access to OHCQ and Adult or Child Protective Services complaint procedures

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Internal complaint process with client notice and timely handling of written complaints
Investigation report with time, date, place, people, description, disposition and prevention
Provide OHCQ complaint hotline 800-492-6005
Reports go to OHCQ immediately on request
Medicaid complaints are reported within 24 hours

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Records released only with written consent or as permitted by Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3
Safeguards against loss, destruction and unauthorized use
Notice of privacy practices given at admission
Staff trained on confidentiality
Breaches are investigated and reported per HIPAA breach rules

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Freedom from exploitation is a client right
No gifts, loans or handling of client money without written policy
Suspected exploitation is reported to local department of social services immediately
Representative payee and POA actions are documented

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: No discrimination based on race, color, national origin, disability, age or sex
Interpreter and translation services at no charge
Reasonable accommodations for disability
Notice of nondiscrimination in the client packet

policies.title: Service Agreement, Cost Estimate, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: Written cost estimate and statement of costs not covered by third parties
Itemized bills on request
Private rate should not be set below the Medicaid rate if billing Medicaid (lesser-of rule)
Disclose subcontract relationships
Medicaid rates posted: $6.3962 per 15 min W5519/W5527

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
state_specifics: COMAR 10.07.05.15: keep client records 5 years after discharge; minors until age 21 or 5 years, whichever is later
Medicaid: keep service documentation 6 years from date of service; use the longer period
Complete discharged records within 30 days of discharge
If the agency closes, return records to client or representative or retain as required
Safeguard against loss and unauthorized use

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Incident and complaint reports within 24 hours, written within 7 days (Medicaid)
Annual OHCQ data collection survey at renewal
HCBS Cost Survey due December 31, 2026
Annual PCA wage report to the Department of Labor by September 1
45 days' notice of ownership, location, name or tax ID change

documents.title: Application for a Residential Service Agency License (Instructions, Section B 'Policies and Procedures' grid, and Required Attachment 3)
documents.form_number: None printed on the form. The file is APPLICATION_RSA-License-06.26.2026-A.pdf, 12 pages.
documents.issuer: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ)
documents.version: File dated 06.26.2026-A. It is the version linked from the OHCQ RSA page.
documents.how_used: This is the official OHCQ document for reviewing a new RSA's policies. Required Attachment 3 requires policies and procedures as specified in COMAR 10.07.05.08B. The 'Policies and Procedures' grid on pages 4-6 lists each required policy under five headings. For each item the applicant names the attached document and its page numbers, or enters N/A if a waiver is requested. The application form's own text is used for the item wording.

documents.title: COMAR 10.07.05.08 Administration (B. Policies and Procedures)
documents.issuer: Maryland Division of State Documents (Library of Maryland Regulations), for OHCQ/MDH
documents.version: Current online text as fetched; the page shows no effective date.
documents.how_used: This is the regulation behind the application grid. Its numbering, B(1)(a)(i) through B(1)(e)(v), supplies the item IDs, because the application grid has no numbers. COMAR 10.07.05.04A(2)(i) requires copies of these policies with the license application. COMAR 10.07.05.04I(3) requires renewal applicants to submit policies that have changed substantively.

required_items.cite: Application p.4 (Policies and Procedures > Administration); COMAR 10.07.05.08B(1)(a)(i)

required_items.text: Administration - Delineation of services provided by the agency when the agency coordinates care within the agency or with another provider

Informed Consent - A client or client representative with legal authority to make legal decisions, signs an informed consent form consenting to changes to the agency’s recommended plan of care; or:

official.notes: OHCQ publishes no separate policy checklist for RSAs. The policy requirements are the 'Policies and Procedures' grid in the RSA License Application (pp.4-6) and COMAR 10.07.05.08B, which the application cites. The application also requires a business plan (including a description of agency services), an organizational chart, an SDAT letter of good standing and workers' compensation proof. These are not policy content and are excluded here. How the reviewer expects submission: (1) Submit a typed application, with the policies and the other attachments, through the OHCQ 'Submit a License Application' link. The application says handwritten applications are returned, and that there is no application fee. (2) Submit the policies as attachments. In each grid box, list the name of the attached document and the page numbers where that policy appears. Organize the manual under the five headings above, in the same order. This makes it easy to cross-reference every B(1) item. (3) To request a waiver of any item, list the policy in the waiver box and explain why it is inappropriate or unnecessary for this RSA. Then enter N/A in that item's box. This follows COMAR 10.07.05.08B(2). (4) Agencies that provide invasive equipment or supplies must arrange 24-hour-a-day equipment maintenance service (COMAR 10.07.05.08B(3)). The application asks about this as a yes/no question. (5) The RSA Certification on worker classification of personal care aides is a separate online form under Health-General §19-4A-11. All applicants must complete it, including those that will not hire personal care aides. (6) Branch offices use the parent's policies. Adding a new home health care service later requires the full application again, with policies for the new service. (7) At renewal, submit any policies that changed substantively, including those on complaint handling and client evaluation and assessment (COMAR 10.07.05.04I(3)). (8) Limits of this result: the grid is built around home health care services, so a non-medical RSA may request waivers for items such as drug administration and enteral/parenteral nutrition. The application does not list COMAR's other chapter requirements, such as the complaint process (.09), screening (.10) and training (.11), as grid items, and I did not fetch those sections. I also did not review the Medicaid program rules (COMAR 10.09.84 and 10.09.20) for additional written-policy requirements.
